content.text:
By the rivers of Babylon, there we sat down,
yea, we wept, when we remembered Zion.
We hanged our harps upon the willows
in the midst thereof.
For there they that carried us away captive
required of us a song;
and they that wasted us required of us mirth,
saying, Sing us one of the songs of Zion.
How shall we sing the LORD’s song
in a strange land?
If I forget thee, O Jerusalem,
let my right hand forget her cunning.
If I do not remember thee,
let my tongue cleave to the roof of my mouth;
if I prefer not Jerusalem
above my chief joy.

questions.q: How many pairs of sheep did Noah take into the ark?
questions.explain: 7 pairs – sheep are clean animals, so Noah took 7 pairs of them; of unclean animals (such as pigs) he took only one pair.

questions.q: Who was freed from prison by an angel in Acts 12?
questions.explain: Peter – the angel led him at night out of the prison where Herod had locked him up.

questions.q: Who was the first to see the risen Jesus?
questions.explain: Mary Magdalene – she was the first to come to the tomb in the morning and she met the risen Jesus.

questions.q: Which book of the New Testament was written first?
questions.explain: 1 Thessalonians – Paul wrote it around AD 50–51, while the Gospels and Acts were written only in the 60s–90s.

questions.q: According to Psalm 137, what is better than forgetting Jerusalem? (see the verses above)
options: To have his eye put out and his right hand cut off
That his right hand forget its skill and his tongue cleave to the roof of his mouth
questions.explain: See verses 5–6: “If I forget thee, O Jerusalem, let my right hand forget her cunning. If I do not remember thee, let my tongue cleave to the roof of my mouth…”
